A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on trace validity, distribution similarity, synthetic-data utility, instruction following, downstream prediction and infilling, plus appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an analysis of exact matches between generated traces and training data in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same text encoding, recursive layer and next-condition generation, and instruction tuning with intermediate reasoning. Training objectives and downstream adaptations are retained; the memorization analysis introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both use Alibaba v2022 traces for the same generation, microservice-management, instruction-following, prediction, and infilling tasks. The new memorization analysis reuses existing evaluation outputs. Operating-system call graphs are discussed as future work, not evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including GReaT, TVAE, the Alibaba probabilistic model, real-data training, and the Llama-2 7B and Llama-3.1 405B comparisons. The new memorization analysis reuses the three variants already compared in Section 4.1.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 adds an evaluation procedure measuring exact training-set matches in graph structure and edge attributes across decoding temperatures. Existing sample counts and splits are retained, sometimes relocated to Appendix B. Figure 4b's change from Accuracy to Similarity labels the same heavy-hitter comparison.

E4.justification: v2 adds a targeted memorization analysis asking whether generated traces reproduce training examples. The earlier structural heatmaps, intermediate-instruction ablation, model-size sensitivity study, and additional distribution and synthetic-data utility analyses remain after renumbering.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 retains five-run averaging but changes the repetition description from varying random seeds or test datasets to varying random seeds. The twenty heavy-hitter runs and existing error bars remain. No increased run count or new uncertainty-estimation method is reported.

E6.justification: New Figure 15 shows only a few percent exact training-trace overlap for recursive variants, versus roughly one-fifth for Baseline. Existing benchmark charts and Table 2 retain their scores. Section 4.1 also corrects instruction-tuning accuracy described as increasing from 23% to 36% into gains of 23% to 36%, without changing Figure 3.

T1.justification: The encoding definitions, layer partition, conditional factorization, and graph-validity constraints are equivalent. v1 Equation 1 becomes inline mathematics in v2 Section 3.1.2. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: The central generation, realism, synthetic-data utility, and downstream-task claims remain. However, the conclusion strengthens broader applicability from v1's holds promise to v2's broadly applies to similarly structured system traces, despite unchanged domain coverage.

C2.justification: v2 expands limitations concerning historical-trace compression and the usefulness of automatically generated instructions, and explicitly identifies transfer to deeper, more heterogeneous operating-system call graphs as untested. Appendix D.3 interprets lower exact-match rates as supporting diversity. The privacy caveat remains in Appendix B.2, but the proposed differential-privacy follow-up is removed.

D1.justification: v2 omits the 99th-percentile labeling rule, default FIRM/TraceVAE hyperparameter statement, SDV implementation disclosure, and supplementary-script statement. It retains the repository link, hardware, LoRA settings, and Table 1, while clarifying that four epochs refers to instruction tuning and adding a model-license note. These are documentation changes, not established implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dubey et al.'s Llama 3 reference and Amazon, Netflix, and Uber sources, while removing Patki et al., Vaswani et al., and Yu et al. The principal positioning against earlier trace and tabular generators remains; Other Related Work is relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, method explanations, and evaluation prose are extensively rewritten and condensed. The contribution bullets are absorbed into prose, related work moves to Appendix A, limitations move into the main text, and experimental details are reorganized into Appendix B.

P2.justification: The document switches from a single-column preprint layout to two columns. Figure 2 is redrawn, Figures 6–7 change proportions and labels, Figure 4b's axis is relabeled, and training-distribution panels are restacked. Figures and tables are extensively relocated, and a new memorization chart is added.

improvement.justification: The memorization analysis provides additional evidence for the central diversity claim, the Figure 3 prose is corrected, and limitations become more concrete. These yield a modest overall improvement. Benefits are tempered by omitted labeling and implementation details and the conclusion's stronger applicability wording, which exceeds the evaluated domain.
